name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,840

entries.clue: Good sort speaks: does so with spasmodic repetition? (8)

blocks.note: a saint is a good sort, and St is how a saint's name is written on a church or a street sign
to utter a word is to speak it

annotation.surface: A decent man opens his mouth, and the sentence asks how the words come out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Does so' points straight back at 'speaks', so the definition borrows the wordplay's own verb and the clue ends up describing itself. The colon is the hinge between the two halves.
annotation.definitionFit: To stutter is to speak with the involuntary repetition of a sound, which is exactly the spasmodic repeating the definition names.

entries.clue: Country girl entered in spelling competition? (6)

indicatorNotes.entered in: To enter a room is to go inside it, so the name in front is written between the letters of what follows.

blocks.note: a spelling bee is the contest American schools run, and those three letters part to take the rest
Liz is a girl's name, the short form of Elizabeth

annotation.surface: A country girl signing herself up for the school spelling bee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country girl' looks like one phrase and is doing two jobs: the first word defines and the second is a name to be planted. The spelling bee is an American institution rather than a British one.
annotation.definitionFit: Belize is the small English-speaking state on the Caribbean coast of Central America, so 'country' names it plainly.

entries.clue: Failing Tesla right — fast beginning to question? (5,5)

indicatorNotes.Failing: Something failing is coming apart under you, and letters coming apart do not stay in the order they were handed over in.

blocks.note: five letters to be re-set
R is the standard short form of right
four more letters joining the same shuffle

annotation.surface: An electric car breaking down at the very moment it should be pulling away quickly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Failing' wants to be the definition — a failing is a fault — but it is the instruction, and the last three words do the defining. A sprinter called back has made a beginning nobody will accept.
annotation.definitionFit: A false start is a start disallowed and taken again, so it is precisely a beginning that is open to question.

entries.clue: Toxin from French fish, a second discarded (6)

indicatorNotes.discarded: What is discarded is thrown away and not kept, so the letter named just before it never reaches the answer.

blocks.note: poisson is the French for fish
s is the short form of second, and this is the letter thrown out

annotation.surface: A toxin drawn from a French fish once part of the catch has been thrown away.
annotation.walkthrough: The French word and the English answer sit one letter apart, which is the whole of the trick and the reason the clue has to name the letter that goes. 'A second' is the unit, not the next fish along.
annotation.definitionFit: A toxin is a poison, though strictly one of biological origin, and the crossword treats the two nouns as interchangeable.

entries.clue: Lorde ultimately inclined to throttle pub trumpeter (8)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: Ultimately means at the very end of things, so only the final letter of the name in front is taken.
indicatorNotes.to throttle: To throttle is to close both hands round a throat, so the word before it shuts round what comes next.

blocks.note: the closing letter of the singer's stage name
someone inclined against a wall has leant on it, and these five letters part to take the next inside
PH is how a public house is marked on an Ordnance Survey map

annotation.surface: The singer Lorde finally leaning over to strangle somebody in a pub.
annotation.walkthrough: Lorde is the New Zealand singer, so 'ultimately' wants the last letter of a stage name and not of a peerage. The definition is a noise rather than a musician: this animal trumpets.
annotation.definitionFit: An elephant trumpets — the blaring call it forces through its trunk — so 'trumpeter' names the animal by the sound it makes.

entries.clue: Side road to turn down endlessly (4)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: Endlessly means with the end gone, so the last letter of the word in front is simply not written.

blocks.note: the five-letter verb for rejecting an offer out of hand
this N is the letter that word ends on, and it is the one dropped

annotation.surface: Refusing something over and over again without ever letting up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turn down' is the rejection and not the direction — nothing in this clue goes downwards. A spur is the short stretch of road that leaves a motorway to reach a town.
annotation.definitionFit: A spur is the short branch road running off a main one, the sense signposted where a motorway feeds a town.

entries.clue: Parrot to be bathed in light: do it twice? Owl was terribly pleased! (4,1,3,4,3,5)

annotation.answer: LIKE A DOG WITH TWO TAILS

indicatorNotes.to be bathed in: To be bathed in something is to be immersed and closed round by it, so the bird's letters end up inside the rest.
indicatorNotes.do it twice: The instruction is meant literally: the word 'it' is written out a second time before anything else happens to the letters.
indicatorNotes.terribly: Terribly means badly, and letters set down badly are letters that have lost the order they came in.

anagram.fodder: KEA LIGHT DO IT IT OWL WAS

blocks.clueFragment: light: do it twice? Owl was
blocks.note: seventeen letters, once the instruction in the middle has been obeyed and 'it' written a second time
the kea is the big green parrot of the New Zealand mountains

annotation.surface: An owl delighted to hear that a parrot is to be washed twice over in the light.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do it twice' is an instruction and not decoration: the word 'it' joins the fodder a second time, and the letters come up short without it. The Owl is Bunter, over at 9.
annotation.definitionFit: To be like a dog with two tails is to be delighted — twice as pleased as a dog can show with the one tail it has for wagging.

entries.clue: See 9
Closed in, misused other half few met almost done with Bunter? (3,3,3,2,3,6)

annotation.answer: THE FAT OWL OF THE REMOVE

indicatorNotes.misused: Something misused has been handled wrongly, and letters handled wrongly come out in the wrong order.
indicatorNotes.almost: Almost stops just short of the thing, so the word it governs arrives without its final letter.

anagram.fodder: TO OTHER HALF FEW MET OVE

blocks.note: a door pushed to is a door closed, and that is the two letters it hands over
fifteen letters to be re-set
when a thing is done it is over, and the word in front stops one letter short of that

annotation.surface: A shut-in man, badly treated, whose other half hardly anybody ever met.
annotation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is Frank Richards's greedy schoolboy at Greyfriars, and the Remove is the form he is stuck in; the answer is what the stories call him throughout. A door 'to' is a door shut.
annotation.definitionFit: The Fat Owl of the Remove is Billy Bunter's standing nickname in the Greyfriars stories — owl for the huge spectacles, Remove for his form.

entries.clue: Say two or three runs one Frenchman gets in games? (5)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition works by example: 'say' warns that the answer names the class two and three belong to rather than either number itself.

indicatorNotes.gets in: What gets in a thing has found its way inside, so the letters just assembled go between the two halves of what follows.

blocks.note: games on a school timetable is PE, physical education, and those two letters part to take the rest
R is runs on a cricket scorecard
I is one in Roman numerals
M is the French abbreviation for Monsieur

annotation.surface: A Frenchman knocking up a couple of runs during the school sports.
annotation.walkthrough: Runs, one and Monsieur each shrink to a single letter, and all three then have to be threaded into the two letters that games gives. 'Say' is the flag for a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A prime is a number divisible only by itself and one, and two and three are the first two of them, so the examples name the class.

entries.clue: See 7
Smashing woman's love for Kent maybe (9)

blocks.note: a smashing afternoon and a super afternoon are the same afternoon
what belongs to a woman is hers, written her
love is nothing in tennis scoring, and nothing is written as a nought

annotation.surface: A terrific woman's affection, aimed at somebody down in Kent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kent' is a county until you remember Clark Kent, which is the whole of the misdirection. 'Smashing' is the dated British adjective for splendid, with nothing broken anywhere.
annotation.definitionFit: Clark Kent is Superman out of costume, so naming him names one example of the kind the answer describes.

entries.clue: Writer's the writer powerless character inspires (7)

indicatorNotes.powerless: Power is P to a physicist, so a word left powerless is that word with its P taken out.
indicatorNotes.inspires: To inspire is literally to breathe in, so the word doing it opens up and draws the other piece into its middle.

blocks.note: a character is a person, and P is the symbol for power, so this one has to go without it
the writer of the clue is the setter, who refers to himself as me

annotation.surface: One author is the writer that some feeble character in a book has inspired.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue says 'writer' twice on purpose: the first is the definition, the second is the setter talking about himself, which in crosswordland is always ME or I. Emerson gave America Self-Reliance and the essays behind it.
annotation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist and poet of Self-Reliance, so 'writer' names him by his trade.

entries.clue: A last look back for Greek maiden (7)

indicatorNotes.back: What is written back is written from its far end, and in an across entry that means reading right to left.

blocks.note: the clue's own letter, staying where it is put
the last of anything is its end
the air somebody has about them is the look of them

annotation.surface: Taking one final glance back over your shoulder.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the two pieces after the opening letter are turned; that A stays put, which is what makes the reversal hard to measure. Ariadne gave Theseus the thread that walked him out of her father's labyrinth at Knossos.
annotation.definitionFit: Ariadne is the Cretan princess of Greek myth who saw Theseus safely out of the labyrinth, a maiden of the legends.

entries.clue: Ostensibly popular celebrity on left unknown (2,4,4)

blocks.note: what is popular this season is in
a big name is a celebrity
the clue's own word, taken at face value for its two letters
L is the short form of left
an unknown quantity in algebra is x, y or z, and y is the one wanted here

annotation.surface: A popular celebrity somewhere on the political left, otherwise unidentified.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' is joining nothing here — it is two of the answer's own letters, lifted straight off the page, which is the step hardest to see. 'Unknown' is algebra's x, y or z.
annotation.definitionFit: Something true in name only is true ostensibly and not in fact: both phrase and adverb mark a claim the reality does not back.

entries.clue: Bird no longer seen on South American islands (5)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is plural and the answer is one country: the name covers a whole South Pacific group rather than any single island in it.

indicatorNotes.on: In an across entry, whatever is written on something has been reached after it, so the bird ends up following the letters it is sitting on.

blocks.note: S is south on the compass
A is the short form of American
the moa was the huge flightless bird of New Zealand, hunted out around 1400

annotation.surface: An extinct bird once found out on some islands off South America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' is the whole instruction: across the grid, a thing written on another sits after it, so the bird comes second in the answer though it comes first in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Samoa is the island group in the South Pacific, so 'islands' names the archipelago the country is made of.

entries.clue: Greek character lay back beside anaemic creature (4,4)

indicatorNotes.back: A word written back is written from its far end, so the three letters in front are read the other way about.

blocks.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
to lay a thing down is to set it down, and these three letters are then turned
somebody anaemic looks wan, pale and washed out

annotation.surface: A Greek fellow lying back next to a pale animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' is the alphabet and not a man from Athens, which is the commonest trap the language offers. The bird here is the heavy orange-billed swan of British rivers and park lakes, and it is not in fact silent.
annotation.definitionFit: A mute swan is a living animal, and 'creature' is the broadest word there is for one, so it covers the swan without narrowing anything.

entries.clue: Start computer deleting an old autonomous program (3)

indicatorNotes.deleting: To delete is to strike out, so the letter named straight after it is the one that does not survive.

blocks.note: to start a computer up is to boot it
O is the short form of old, and this is the letter struck out

annotation.surface: Switching a computer on and wiping something ancient off it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start computer' is verb and object together, and what gets deleted is one letter rather than an old file. A bot is the script that posts, crawls or trades with nobody at the keyboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A bot runs on its own once set going — crawling, posting or trading unattended — which is what the definition means by autonomous.

entries.clue: Many a house in this Manhattan thoroughfare (8)

annotation.definition: Many a house in this Manhattan thoroughfare

blocks.note: read as a street lined with dwellings, and meant as the playhouses standing along it — a house in the trade is the auditorium and the audience in it
the long street cutting diagonally across the island's grid, and the name the whole American commercial theatre goes by

annotation.surface: A street in Manhattan with a great many homes along it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House' is the theatre word — a full house, the house lights — and the forty-odd playhouses along one stretch of this street are what the clue is counting. No fodder anywhere is being shuffled or hidden.
annotation.definitionFit: Broadway is the avenue running the length of Manhattan and also the theatre district along its middle stretch, so both senses of the clue meet in one street.

entries.clue: On booze heading west for river (5)

indicatorNotes.heading west: West is leftwards on any map, so an across answer heading that way is read from its right-hand end back.

blocks.note: a memo headed re this or that is a memo on it
gin is the booze, and both pieces are then set down from the back

annotation.surface: Someone on the drink and making their way westwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' is the word a memo uses, not the preposition the surface wants, and it supplies letters rather than joining anything. The Niger rises in Guinea and loops through Mali and Nigeria to the Atlantic.
annotation.definitionFit: The Niger is the great river of West Africa, third longest on the continent, so 'river' names it by its kind.

entries.clue: Sister to tempestuous Pre-Raphaelite co-founder (8)

indicatorNotes.tempestuous: A tempest throws everything about, so the words in front of it may be taken in any order their letters allow.

blocks.note: eight letters to be re-set

annotation.surface: A sister to some stormy founder of the Pre-Raphaelites.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface happens to be true: Christina Rossetti, the poet of Goblin Market, really was the sister of Dante Gabriel, and they share the surname the letters spell.
annotation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti was one of the young painters who founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood in 1848, so the surname names a founder.

entries.clue: See 7
Immoral women's group on deck soused (6)

indicatorNotes.soused: Soused means drunk, and a drunk's letters will not walk in a straight line, so the four in front come out in some other order.

blocks.note: the WI is the Women's Institute, the British village organisation of jam, talks and committees
four letters re-set to follow on behind

annotation.surface: Some Women's Institute members getting thoroughly pickled up on deck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soused' carries both senses at once — pickled in brine and pickled in drink — and it is the second that tells the letters to move. Pairing it with a village institute is the joke.
annotation.definitionFit: Wicked means morally bad, as a wicked act or a wicked stepmother is bad, so 'immoral' is the plain adjective for it.

entries.clue: Fights in unruly mob tigers must devour? (7)

indicatorNotes.unruly: An unruly crowd keeps no order, so the letters beside the word need not keep theirs either.
indicatorNotes.must devour: To devour is to swallow a thing whole, so the word in front opens up and the other letters go down inside it.

blocks.note: a tiger is a big cat, and those four letters part to take the rest inside
three letters re-set before they go in

annotation.surface: Scuffles breaking out in a rowdy crowd the tigers are expected to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: Three letters have only six possible orders, and just one of them leaves a word once the big cats close round it. Everything after the first word is instruction, though the sentence reads as one continuous scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Combats are fights — armed engagements, or bouts between two people — so the plural noun answers the plural definition exactly.

entries.clue: Load for guns in Light Brigade assault? (6)

blocks.note: read as gunnery: the measured quantity of powder and shot rammed down a barrel before firing
read again as cavalry: the ride the British light horse made at the Russian guns at Balaclava in 1854

annotation.surface: Ammunition for the guns during the Light Brigade's famous attack.
annotation.walkthrough: Guns belong to both halves of the clue, which is why the two definitions sit so comfortably in one sentence. Tennyson's poem is why the Balaclava ride is the assault everybody can name.
annotation.definitionFit: A charge is the measured load of powder put into a gun, and equally a body of horse riding at the enemy at speed, as at Balaclava.

entries.clue: Unearth urn containing son to Pendragon (6)

indicatorNotes.containing: A thing containing another holds it whole and unbroken, so a run of letters sits inside the words in front exactly as they are written.

blocks.note: six letters running on unbroken across the join between the two words

annotation.surface: Digging up an urn with somebody's son inside it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unearth' looks like the instruction and is in fact the fodder; 'containing' is what tells you to extract. Uther Pendragon is the father in Geoffrey of Monmouth's telling, so 'son to' is the whole definition.
annotation.definitionFit: In the legends Arthur is the son Uther Pendragon fathered at Tintagel, so the definition names him by his parentage rather than his kingship.

entries.clue: Woman never believed as in random canards (9)

indicatorNotes.in: What is in a thing sits inside it, so the two letters before this go into the middle of the letters that follow.
indicatorNotes.random: Random order is no order at all, so the word after it may be taken in whatever arrangement is wanted.

blocks.note: seven letters re-set, and then opened up to take the short word inside
the clue's own word, two letters lifted straight off the page

annotation.surface: A woman nobody ever believed, of the kind who turns up in made-up stories.
annotation.walkthrough: A canard is a false report passed off as news, so the surface is all rumour. Apollo gave Cassandra true prophecy and then the curse that nobody would credit a word of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Cassandra foresaw the fall of Troy and was doomed to be disbelieved, so 'woman never believed' is her whole story in three words.

entries.clue: Mistake to ignore leader in church area (4)

indicatorNotes.ignore: To ignore a thing is to pass it over as though it were not there, so the letter named beside it is left out.

blocks.note: a lapse is a slip, a momentary mistake
this L is the letter leading that word, and it is the one passed over

annotation.surface: It is a mistake to overlook the man in charge of a parish.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'leader' a person and the wordplay makes it a letter, the one standing at the front of the word before. An apse is the rounded recess at a church's east end, behind the altar.
annotation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular vaulted recess at the east end of a church, so 'church area' names a part of the building.

entries.clue: See 9
Welshman last to service vehicles (5)

indicatorNotes.last: Last means at the very end, so only the closing letter of the word it points at is taken.

blocks.note: the letter that word finishes on
vans are the vehicles a delivery firm runs

annotation.surface: A Welshman is last in the queue to have his vans serviced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last to service' reads as a place in a queue and means the final letter of the word 'service' itself, which is the step to spot. Evans comes from Evan, the Welsh form of John.
annotation.definitionFit: Evans is one of the handful of surnames, with Jones and Williams, that a Welshman is likeliest to carry, so it names one by example.

entries.clue: PCP from doctor opening time draws in (5,4)

indicatorNotes.draws in: To draw something in is to pull it inside you, so the letters already assembled open up and take the earlier word into the middle.

blocks.note: the anus is an opening of the body, and these four letters part to take the rest
T is the short form of time, joining on the end before anything goes inside
to geld a horse is to castrate it, which is what doctoring an animal means

annotation.surface: Scoring the drug from a doctor just as opening time comes round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the vet's verb here and 'opening' is anatomical rather than a pub's, so both of the clue's innocent words are ruder than they look. Angel dust is the street name for phencyclidine.
annotation.definitionFit: PCP is phencyclidine, and angel dust is the street name the drug has gone by since it spread as a powder in the 1970s.
